reviews.review: I like stealthy games with action.

Let's get this straight: this is not Sniper Elite 6, and it barely feels like a proper DLC to Sniper Elite 5.

I have played every Sniper Elite game, and the modern ones in co-op with a friend. Resistance feels like someone took the Sniper Elite 5 engine exactly as it was, kept all its old bugs, and gave it to a much less experienced gameplay and level design team. That is probably why it is not called Sniper Elite 6.

The biggest problem is the AI. It feels like a considerable regression from Sniper Elite 4 and 5, and it makes the game way too easy.

Enemies never use the alarms. There are alarm systems everywhere for you to disable, but what is the point if nobody ever triggers them? There are basically no reinforcements either, apart from maybe one or two scripted events where a truck arrives with four to six soldiers, and even that is not threatening.

You can just start shooting loudly and enemies often come one by one through the same path until they are all dead. Nobody surrounds you, no serious counterattack develops, and there is almost no feeling that the enemy is reacting intelligently to your presence.

In Sniper Elite 3 to 5, I felt under constant threat. I wanted to stay hidden, break lights, avoid alarms, move bodies, set traps and plan for failure.

That planning mattered because resources and inventory space were limited. Choosing one more mine instead of a bandage mattered. Spending a talent point to carry more equipment mattered.

Here it does not.

There are barely any roaming vehicles, no meaningful reinforcements, and almost no reason to mine a road. At the same time, explosives are everywhere. After looting only a few soldiers or rooms, my inventory is already full of ammo, mines, medical supplies and almost everything else, even on the hardest difficulty. I could practically mine every road on the map, but for what?

The same problem applies to traps. I used to enjoy rigging bodies or preparing an ambush in case a patrol found them later. Here, once the nearby soldiers are dead, almost nobody is coming.

Even VIP targets behave stupidly. Instead of fleeing the map or hiding somewhere secure, which gave you a real reason to remain stealthy in previous games, I have seen scientists grab a gun and come outside to hunt me after I already killed dozens of guards.

So the game gives you more tools than ever while removing most of the situations where those tools were useful. Nothing feels scarce, preparation barely matters, and very little feels rewarding.

Talents have the same problem. You can revive yourself, shoot while downed, carry plenty of supplies and replenish almost everything constantly. Most upgrades simply do not feel important.

Weapons also lack personality. I noticed surprisingly little difference between rifles, ammunition types or many weapon modifications. Even the sniping itself somehow feels less rewarding and more arcade-like than before.

Then there is the HUD, which keeps one of my biggest problems with Sniper Elite 5.

The game offers a million difficulty and realism options, yet there is no sensible middle ground for the HUD. Either I get too much arcade information, including indicators showing when enemies are spotting me and text literally explaining what the AI is doing, or I disable so much that I also lose basic information like my health and remaining ammunition.

And no, "just play without the HUD" does not solve this.

In real life I know how many magazines, grenades and other items I have on my belt or in my backpack. Hiding that information is not realism, especially when the game has no proper tactical inventory screen where I can simply check what I am carrying.

I just want to know my health, ammo and equipment without the game also telling me what every enemy around me is thinking.

Sniping has a similar problem. Even with my sniping settings pushed toward maximum realism, the game still gives too much assistance and too much indication of where the shot should go. Combined with the weak AI and lack of danger, it feels more like an arcade mechanic than something I really had to judge and earn.

Then there are the bugs. Many Sniper Elite 5 bugs are still present, with new ones added. Traps attached to electrical panels sometimes simply do not explode, for example.

The world also feels lifeless. There is little interesting dialogue to overhear, little environmental storytelling, and almost nobody except soldiers waiting to be killed.

The two things I still appreciate are that the campaign can be played entirely in co-op with a friend, and that you can save almost anywhere instantly. Unfortunately, when the game provides so little resistance, even the excellent save system becomes much less important.

I am genuinely disappointed because Sniper Elite is a great series and the basic engine is still very good. But Resistance removes much of what made the previous games interesting: tension, stealth, preparation, scarcity, meaningful loadouts, intelligent enemy reactions and rewarding sniping.

I cannot recommend it, even on sale. I would rather wait and hope Rebellion comes back with a proper Sniper Elite 6.

A Game That Feels Stuck in the Past

Visuals
The game is ugly — noticeably so, and in my opinion far beyond what we saw in Sniper Elite 3 and Sniper Elite 4. It feels visually dated rather than intentionally stylised, which makes it difficult to overlook how little the series appears to have progressed.

Gameplay & Innovation
The biggest problem is how rehashed and tired the experience feels. There is very little here that feels genuinely new, and I haven't seen any meaningful improvements or innovation that justify this feeling like a new entry rather than a retread of what came before.

AI & Immersion
The AI constantly pulls me out of the experience. Enemies will make completely nonsensical decisions — for example, remaining completely unalerted while everyone around them is screaming, scrambling for cover, and engaging in a firefight. Moments like this make it impossible to stay immersed because the game repeatedly reminds you that you're fighting against a collection of scripted behaviours rather than believable enemies.

Music & Atmosphere
The music also feels like it was carried over from the previous game rather than designed around this one. It doesn't fit the environments particularly well and often feels disconnected from the atmosphere the game is trying to create.

Bugs
I'm actually writing this review because I've encountered a game-breaking bug where my weapon has become stuck in an infinite reload loop and can no longer be used. It's an especially frustrating way to be reminded of how rough around the edges the game feels.

Overall
Overall, this feels like a great game from 2009 that somehow never got the memo that it's now 2026. The core concept is still enjoyable, but the dated visuals, lack of meaningful innovation, questionable AI, mismatched music, and game-breaking bugs make it feel like the series has failed to keep up with the times.

Try Sniper Elite 4. its the same game., but it looks prettier.
